transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you might have about your cataract surgery and recovery.

Is there anything you'd like to know about how you're getting on since your operation?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a great question! You can start doing some light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. So gardening counts as light exercise, which is fine to do from that point onwards.

However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for about a month after your operation.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I was wondering when I can start using my eye gel for dry eyes again?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question. It's safe to continue using your eye gel for dry eyes - you can use it unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

If you're running out of it, your GP should be able to provide you with more.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain when it's bright, or severe light sensitivity - especially if your eye is also red and painful - that's not normal, and we may need to assess this further. In that case, please let your care team know.

Does that help? Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, one more question: Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That depends on how long it's been since your surgery. It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after your operation, but this should improve quickly and settle down over time.

How many days or weeks has it been since your surgery? That will help me give you a better answer about whether what you're experiencing is normal.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It's been about two weeks since my surgery.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Thank you for letting me know. By two weeks, your vision should be improving and becoming clearer. Some mild blurriness can still be present, but it should be getting better.

However, if your vision is still quite blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay. So if you're concerned about how clear your vision is at this point, it's worth mentioning to your care team.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's all the questions I had. Thank you so much for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, all my questions have been answered. Thanks again for your help!

verdict.label: pass
